entry.content:

The Defense of Banks — A Timeline ✅ Verified

YearWhat She DidQuote / Source
2015Organized education tour where Banks participatedLegislative records
2015Both declined to vote to expel Reps. Courser/Gamrat — same “due process” stance as BanksMI House records
2016PUBLICLY RALLIED FOR BANKS when AG Schuette filed felony charges“These attacks will not be tolerated. Who was allowed to go through the records and find this? I believe it was his opponent.” — Detroit News
2017Defended Banks’ plea deal“For him to have charges for a loan that was paid back in excess of what the original loan was is very disheartening… Brian has been a fighter for Detroit Public Schools.” — FOX 2, MI Chronicle
2020Sought Kwame Kilpatrick clemency from Trump at White HouseDetroit Free Press, IndyStar
2021–2025DPSCD Board Member — sat on the board that authorized PCADPSCD records
2025Named PCA “development team” to Chalkbeat — including Judge Miller and AAG MorelandChalkbeat
Sep 30, 2025Appointed Detroit Ombudsman — resigned DPSCD within 48 hoursBridgeDetroit

She defended Banks at every stage: when he was charged, when he pled, when he needed a charter. Then she took a 10-year appointment that makes her nearly unfireable.

Direct Payments to Banks Network ✅ Verified

From PACToAmountYearSource
Strong Women Lead PACJoseph Holland Jr.$1,5002018TransparencyUSA
Strong Women Lead PACJoseph Holland Jr.$5002022TransparencyUSA
CampaignTenisha Yancey District Judge$2502022TransparencyUSA

$2,000 to a convicted drug trafficker (Holland: 2 felony drug trafficking convictions, MDOC discharge “WITHOUT IMPROVEMENT”). What “services” did Holland provide to a state representative’s PAC?

AG Referral — Same Pattern as Banks ✅ Verified

EntityReferredYearSource
“Dagnogo For Jobs And Edu” (ID 515680)MI Attorney GeneralOct 2023MI SOS referral list
Banks’ PACs (multiple)MI Attorney GeneralOct 2023MI SOS referral list

Both Gay-Dagnogo and Banks had their campaign committees referred to the Michigan AG for failure to file in the same month of the same year. Same pattern, same noncompliance, same network.

Banks Named Her ✅ Verified

In It Had 2 Happen, Banks thanks “State Representative Sherry Gay-Dagnogo” by name in his acknowledgments — alongside Karen Dumas and Todd Perkins.

When a convicted felon writes a book and names you as someone he’s grateful to, and you then authorize his charter school while paying his convicted drug trafficker associate from your campaign fund, the book becomes evidence.

The Golden Parachute 📄 Documented 

2015-2020: State Rep HD-8
    ├── Publicly defended Banks at AG charges
    ├── Defended Banks' plea deal
    ├── Paid Holland $2,000 from PAC
    │
2021-2025: DPSCD Board
    ├── Authorized PCA's charter
    ├── Named development team (Miller, Moreland)
    ├── AG-referred for campaign finance failure
    │
Oct 2025: RESIGNED DPSCD → Ombudsman
    ├── 48-hour turnaround
    ├── 10-year term to 2035
    ├── $199,500/year
    ├── Cannot easily be removed
    └── Now handles citizen complaints about city departments
        └── INCLUDING complaints about DPSCD

If a Detroit resident complains about DPSCD’s authorization of Banks’ schools, that complaint routes through Gay-Dagnogo’s office — the same person who authorized those schools, paid Banks’ associate, and publicly defended Banks at every legal proceeding.

The complaint system itself has been captured.

The Kilpatrick Connection

Gay-Dagnogo has a documented pattern of defending convicted public officials:

OfficialCrimeGay-Dagnogo’s Action
Brian Banks9 convictions (6 felony)Rallied (2016), defended plea (2017), authorized charter (2025)
Kwame Kilpatrick24 federal felonies, RICOSought clemency from Trump at White House (2020)

She doesn’t just enable — she advocates for convicted officials. She frames accountability as attack: “These attacks will not be tolerated.” She reframes fraud as injustice: “A loan that was paid back.” She describes prosecution as persecution.

This is the racial solidarity shield at its most explicit. The AG who charged Banks was (Republican) Bill Schuette. Gay-Dagnogo framed the charges as political opposition — “I believe it was his opponent” — turning criminal prosecution into a racial solidarity issue.
